sentences.text: Task 4. The committee chose Krakow in Poland to be Hong Kong’s twin city.
Let me, Chan visit it.
crack off for three months and has returned to Brunch with Charlie to talk about her experiences.
Listen to the interview and answer the questions below.
Please note you do not need to answer in complete sentences.
You now have 30 seconds to study the task.
At the end of the task, you will have three minutes to tidy up your answers.
it’s time for our special guest today.
Today I’m very happy to have back Ms Lemme Chan from Hong Kong University.
Thank you. Now, I've never been to Poland or Krakow and I’m sure a lot of our listeners haven’t either.
So maybe to start with, what were your first impressions of Krakow?
Well, from the moment I first arrived, the people in Krakow were really generous.
Right. I mean, I lived with a host family, you know, and they were so generous and so were their friends In what way?
Well, I mean, everyone invited me into their homes, and you know, made me feel just very welcome.
It was very different to Hong Kong.
I mean, here you don’t normally get invited to someone’s home.
You were saying before before we came on air that it can be pretty cold in Poland.
So was the weather cold all the time?
Sometimes the temperature got down to minus 32 degrees!
Wow, how did you cope!
Well actually it wasn’t that bad.
When you’re inside, the heating’s turned on all the time.
And Sometimes it’s actually too warm and you have to open a window.
What? Even when it’s minus 32 outside?
Yeah, exactly! And when you are outside you wear thermal underwear, you know, like that special winter underwear, so you're always warm.
So if you do visit Poland in winter take your thermal underwear that’s my advice.
Well, you've heard it here first listeners!
So you said your host family were nice.
What about people in general?
Actually, most people were very friendly.
Only most You make it sound like some people weren't.
No, not at all, not at all, though there was one particular incident.
Oh yes, and what happened then?
Well, I was in a cafe and I was ordering something to drink.
And I said to the waiter in Polish, I said dvah habata prussia which means in Polish two teas please And the waiter said de vie.
Apparently, I had made a grammatical mistake when I said the word for two and he the waiter, I mean seemed actually quite angry about it.
It was like if you are going to speak our language then you must speak it properly!
I was so shocked and embarrassed.
There was me trying my best to speak Polish and he was so intolerant.
Apparently, everything had to be grammatically perfect.
At least I was trying to speak the language!
Hmm. and you were telling me earlier about a big adventure you had on your skiing trip.
Oh, yes. And actually, this is a better example of how nice the people in Poland are.
Me and the daughter of the host family, Julia, we decided to go skiing.
Actually we tried to go the Sunday before but we got this really really slow train on the Sunday morning that stopped everywhere.
I think it stopped at 52 different stations!
So by the time we got there it was too late to ski.
So the next Sunday we decided to get the bus instead.
And was that better than the train?
Yeah, much better.
We got there by 9 in the morning.
morning. So had you ever skied before then?
No, I hadn't.
No, neither have I.
How did you find it?
Well, if you've never been skiing, there are easy slopes for beginners and children.
So I was on the easy slopes in the morning and that was OK, but then after lunch I got on the wrong lift and ended up at the top of a really difficult slope.
Oh no! And there was no way down except to ski down!
Oh no! And did you fall?
Yeah! Again and again.
I thought I was going to die.
I was terrified!
Well, you’re braver than I would have been.
I don’t know about that.
I got to the bottom and I didn’t ski again.
I just sat in the cafe and drank hot chocolate all afternoon.
So that was your ski adventure.
Well, actually, that wasn’t all.
So what else happened?
Well, we were on the bus coming back and it was late evening.
We were about an hour from Krakow, the weather was really bad.
I mean, lots of snow, and the bus broke down.
Oh dear! It wouldn’t have been that bad but I was actually going to give a talk about Hong Kong to a school in Krakow at 9 o 'clock in the morning the day after on the Monday morning, and
I really didn’t want to miss the talk and let everyone down.
Oh no. So what happened next?
Well, as luck would have it, the host family had a cousin who lived nearby, and Julia called him and he said he would help us.
And did he?
Did you get back on time for your talk?
Actually I did.

And you're not going to believe this, and I’m not sure I believe it myself, but the cousin was a farmer and after Julia called him, we waited and waited waited and waited and finally he turned up in his
tractor! His tractor!
Yeah and he drove us all the way back to Krakow in his tractor.
It turns out the tractors are really great for travelling in heavy snow.
It took us about three hours but we got back to Krakow and I managed to make it in time for my talk.
I mean, it was really nice of him.
The cousin, Well that’s a great story.
OK, so thanks again Lemmy, for dropping in.
